turns.text: We've got a week off in spring and want somewhere warm, but not a twelve hour flight.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Lisbon, Seville or one of the Greek islands would all fit. Are you more in the mood for a city or a beach?

welcome_back: Welcome back! We were planning your spring week. City or beach?
Hi again. You were deciding between a city trip and somewhere with a beach.
There you are. Did you settle on city or beach for spring?

endings.user: City, definitely. I get bored lying on the sand.
endings.moshi: Then Lisbon is a great pick. Lots of walking, good food and day trips to the coast if you change your mind.

endings.user: Beach. We need a proper rest this time.
endings.moshi: A Greek island it is. Crete is easy to reach and still quiet in spring.

turns.text: I found two flights to Tokyo. One is cheaper but has a nine hour layover.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: That layover is long, but you could leave the airport for a few hours. Is saving the money worth the extra travel time to you?

Hey, good to have you back. Did you decide whether the long layover is worth the savings?

endings.user: Yeah, I'll take the cheap one. I'm a student, every bit counts.
endings.moshi: Makes sense. Bring a neck pillow and check whether you need a transit visa to leave the airport.

endings.user: No, I'll pay more. I hate airports.
endings.moshi: Fair enough. You'll arrive much fresher, and that first day in Tokyo is worth a lot.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Help me pack for a long weekend in Edinburgh in October.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: It'll be cool and probably rainy. First, carry-on only, or are you checking a bag?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Oh, I hadn't thought about that.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: It changes what you can bring, so it's worth deciding now.

think_reask: So, carry-on only or a checked bag for Edinburgh?
Have you decided on the bag situation for your trip?
welcome_back: Welcome back! We were packing for Edinburgh. Carry-on only, or checking a bag?
Hi again. Still thinking about carry-on versus a checked bag?

endings.user: Carry-on. I don't want to wait at baggage claim.
endings.moshi: Good. Wear your bulkiest jacket and boots on the plane, and pack layers you can mix.

endings.user: I'll check a bag, I always bring too much.
endings.moshi: No judgment. Then pack a proper raincoat and an extra pair of shoes in case one gets soaked.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: {friend}, when does your passport expire? I need to check before I book anything.

turns.speaker: friend
turns.text: Uh, sometime next year I think. Let me look.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Some countries want six months left on it, so it matters.

turns.speaker: friend
turns.text: Okay, found it. It's good until next August.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Perfect, that works. Mine's fine too.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Do you care if we stay in a hotel or would you rather rent an apartment?

turns.speaker: friend
turns.text: Apartment, if it has a kitchen. Eating out every night gets expensive.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: True. But hotels usually have breakfast included.

turns.speaker: friend
turns.text: We can buy croissants. Honestly I just want a balcony.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Ha, okay, balcony and kitchen. I'll filter for that.

turns.speaker: friend
turns.text: And not too far from the train station please, with all our bags.

turns.text: Hey {friend}, can you drive us to the airport on Friday morning?

turns.speaker: friend

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: What's the best way to get from Paris to Amsterdam?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: The train is easiest. It takes a bit over three hours and drops you right in the city center.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Is it expensive?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: It can be if you book late. Book a few weeks ahead and you'll often find much cheaper fares.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: What about flying? It's only / like an hour in the air, right?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: About an hour, yes, but with getting to the airport and security it usually ends up slower than the train.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Okay, train it is. Should I stop somewhere on the way?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Brussels or Antwerp make a nice stop. You could spend an afternoon there and catch a later train.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I'm taking my two kids on their first flight next month. Any tips?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Bring snacks, headphones and something new for each of them to unwrap on the plane. Novelty buys you a lot of quiet time.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Ha, good one. They're four and seven. Will their ears hurt?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Sometimes during takeoff and landing. Chewing or drinking through a straw really helps.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Should I get seats near the front or / actually, does it matter?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Near the front means getting off faster, which is nice with tired kids. Window seats keep them entertained too.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: And can I bring their car seat?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Most airlines let you check it for free. Some approved seats can even be used on board, so ask your airline.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Do I need travel insurance for a short trip inside Europe?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: It's not required, but it's cheap and covers things like cancellations and lost luggage. Worth it for peace of mind.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: My credit card might already include some. How do I check?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Look in your card's benefits page or call them. Often you have to pay for the trip with that card for it to count.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I paid for the hotel with it but the flights / hmm, I think with my debit card.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Then the flights might not be covered. A basic policy just for the trip could fill that gap.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Got it. Thanks, that's really helpful.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: You're welcome. Have a great trip!

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: My wife and I want to do a road trip along the coast for our anniversary. How many days should we plan?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: That depends on the distance, but five to seven days usually lets you drive a few hours a day and still enjoy the stops.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: We're not in a hurry. We're both retired.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Then take your time. Two nights in the nicest spots makes it feel like a holiday instead of a race.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Should we book the hotels in advance or / just see where we end up?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Book the weekends and any popular towns ahead. Weekdays you can usually find something on the day.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: That's a good balance. Anything special for an anniversary?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Pick one night with a really good dinner and a view. Mention the anniversary when you book, places often add a little surprise.
